generic.name: Condition not in knowledge base
generic.summary: The model predicted a class that is not in this website's knowledge base yet, so no detailed explanation is available.
generic.symptoms: Compare the symptoms in your photo with the predicted label.
causes: Cannot be determined automatically for this class.
control: Isolate the affected plants and take clear photos of the leaf front/back, stem and fruit.
Ask a local agricultural extension officer or agronomist to confirm the diagnosis before any treatment.
prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and keep tools clean.
generic.fertilizer: Apply fertilizer according to a soil test; avoid excess nitrogen on stressed plants.

diseases.name: Healthy plant
diseases.summary: The model sees no sign of the diseases it was trained on.
control: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring, especially after rain or heavy irrigation.
prevention: Keep balanced irrigation and nutrition, scout weekly, remove debris.
diseases.fertilizer: Maintain the normal balanced NPK programme for the crop and growth stage, guided by soil tests.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.summary: A fast-spreading disease of potato and tomato that destroys leaves, stems and tubers/fruit within days under cool, wet conditions.
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green blotches that turn brown-black, often with white fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather.
causes: Cool (about 10-24 C) and very humid or rainy weather.
Infected seed tubers, volunteer plants or nearby infected fields.
Long periods of leaf wetness and dense canopy.
control: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants or parts (do not compost).
Use a locally registered fungicide programme (protectant plus systemic products) strictly following the label.
Avoid overhead irrigation and irrigate early in the day.
prevention: Certified disease-free seed, resistant varieties, wide spacing, 3-year rotation, destroy cull piles.
diseases.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen (soft, dense growth is more susceptible); keep phosphorus and potassium adequate. Follow a soil test.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.summary: A common fungal leaf disease of tomato and potato that mainly affects older, stressed leaves and reduces yield by cutting photosynthesis.
diseases.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on lower leaves, surrounded by yellowing; may spread to stems and fruit.
causes: Warm (about 24-29 C), humid weather with alternating wet and dry periods.
Spores surviving on infected crop debris and soil.
Plant stress, especially low nitrogen or heavy fruit load.
control: Remove infected lower leaves and crop debris.
Use protectant fungicides (e.g. chlorothalonil, mancozeb or copper-based) as allowed locally, following label rates.
Water at the base of plants, not over the foliage.
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 2-3 years, use certified seed, stake and space plants for airflow, mulch to reduce soil splash.
diseases.fertilizer: Keep a balanced NPK supply: avoid nitrogen deficiency (weak plants are more susceptible) but also avoid excess. Potassium and calcium support tissue strength. Follow a soil test.

diseases.name: Bacterial spot
diseases.summary: A bacterial disease of tomato, pepper and stone fruits that causes leaf spotting, defoliation and blemished fruit.
diseases.symptoms: Small dark, water-soaked spots that become angular or round with yellow halos; rough scabby spots on fruit.
causes: Warm, wet, windy weather that splashes bacteria between plants.
Contaminated seed or transplants.
Working in the field when plants are wet.
control: Remove badly infected plants; avoid handling plants while wet.
Copper-based bactericides can slow spread (often combined with mancozeb); effectiveness is limited, follow the local label.
Use drip irrigation instead of sprinklers.
prevention: Pathogen-free seed and transplants, crop rotation, clean tools, resistant varieties.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced nutrition; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure calcium supply for stronger tissue. Follow a soil test.

diseases.name: Leaf mould
diseases.summary: A fungal disease of tomato, mostly in greenhouses or very humid fields, that damages leaves from underneath.
diseases.symptoms: Pale green-yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-brown velvety mould on the underside.
causes: Relative humidity above about 85%.
Poor ventilation and dense canopy.
Moderate temperatures (20-25 C).
control: Increase ventilation and lower humidity; remove affected leaves.
Use locally registered fungicides if pressure is high.
prevention: Resistant varieties, wider spacing, pruning, avoiding wet foliage.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid excess nitrogen that creates dense, humid canopies.

diseases.name: Septoria leaf spot
diseases.summary: A fungal leaf spot of tomato that causes heavy leaf loss and sun-scald of fruit.
diseases.symptoms: Many small circular spots with grey-white centres and dark borders, starting on lower leaves.
causes: Warm, wet weather and splashing water.
Infected debris and weeds of the same plant family.
control: Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation.
Protectant fungicides per local recommendation.
prevention: Rotation (2-3 years), mulching, weed control, clean debris after harvest.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced NPK with adequate potassium; avoid nitrogen excess.

diseases.name: Target spot
diseases.summary: A fungal disease causing leaf, stem and fruit lesions on tomato and other crops.
diseases.symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric rings and a yellow halo.
causes: Warm, humid conditions with long leaf wetness.
Infected residue.
control: Remove infected leaves and debris; improve airflow.
Locally registered fungicides if needed.
prevention: Rotation, spacing, drip irrigation.

diseases.name: Spider mite infestation
diseases.summary: Tiny sap-sucking mites that multiply fastest in hot, dry weather and cause stippling and leaf drying.
diseases.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling, bronzing, fine webbing under leaves, leaf drop.
causes: Hot (above about 28 C) and dry conditions.
Dusty fields and water-stressed plants.
Overuse of broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies.
control: Spray water forcefully under leaves, use insecticidal soap or horticultural oil, or a registered miticide (rotate modes of action).
Release predatory mites where practical.
prevention: Avoid water stress, reduce dust, scout leaf undersides weekly.
diseases.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen, which boosts mite reproduction; keep potassium adequate and irrigation regular.

diseases.name: Yellow leaf curl virus
diseases.agent: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci)
diseases.summary: A virus with no cure that stunts plants and drastically cuts yield; controlled by managing the whitefly vector.
diseases.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf edges, small leaves, stunted plants, few fruit.
causes: Feeding by infected whiteflies.
Warm weather that increases whitefly populations.
Infected transplants and nearby weeds.
control: Remove and destroy infected plants early.
Control whiteflies: yellow sticky traps, insect-proof nets, rotation of registered insecticides.
prevention: Resistant/tolerant varieties, virus-free transplants, weed control, reflective mulch.
diseases.fertilizer: Nutrition cannot cure a virus; keep balanced fertilisation to help plants tolerate stress.

diseases.name: Mosaic virus
diseases.summary: A very stable virus spread mechanically by hands, tools and contaminated seed; there is no chemical cure.
diseases.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling, distorted narrow leaves, stunting, uneven fruit ripening.
causes: Contaminated seed, tools, hands or clothing.
Infected plant debris.
control: Remove and destroy infected plants; wash hands and disinfect tools.
Do not handle tobacco before touching plants.
prevention: Certified seed, resistant varieties, sanitation, rotation.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced nutrition only supports tolerance; it does not cure the virus.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.summary: A fungal disease that grows on the leaf surface and reduces photosynthesis; unlike most fungi it does not need free water on the leaf.
diseases.symptoms: White to grey powdery coating on leaves and shoots, later yellowing and curling.
causes: Moderate temperatures with high humidity but a dry leaf surface.
Dense, shaded canopy and poor airflow.
control: Sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or locally registered fungicides at first signs; remove heavily infected parts.
prevention: Resistant varieties, pruning for airflow, avoid excess nitrogen.
diseases.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen (lush tissue is more susceptible); adequate potassium helps.

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.summary: A group of fungi producing rust-coloured pustules that drain the plant of nutrients.
diseases.symptoms: Orange to brown pustules on leaves (or yellow-orange spots on apple leaves for cedar apple rust).
causes: Wind-blown spores, mild temperatures and dew or humidity.
Alternate host plants nearby (e.g. juniper for cedar apple rust).
control: Fungicide at early infection per local label; remove alternate hosts where possible.
prevention: Resistant varieties, early planting, field sanitation.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure potassium.

diseases.name: Apple scab
diseases.summary: The most important fungal disease of apple, causing leaf spots and rough, cracked fruit.
diseases.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit that become corky.
causes: Cool, wet spring weather.
Spores released from fallen infected leaves.
control: Protectant fungicides from bud break under local advisories; remove or shred fallen leaves.
prevention: Resistant cultivars, pruning for airflow, leaf-litter management.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced nutrition; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure calcium for fruit quality.

diseases.name: Esca (black measles)
diseases.agent: Complex of wood-decay fungi (e.g. Phaeomoniella chlamydospora)
diseases.summary: A chronic grapevine trunk disease that causes leaf striping and can lead to vine decline.
diseases.symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf pattern, dark spots on berries, wood discolouration.
causes: Infection through pruning wounds.
Vine stress and old vines.
control: No effective cure: remove infected wood, protect pruning wounds, replace severely affected vines.
prevention: Prune in dry weather, seal wounds, use clean planting material.
diseases.fertilizer: Keep vines well-nourished and irrigated to reduce stress; follow a soil test.

diseases.name: Black rot
diseases.summary: A fungal disease causing leaf spots and mummified, black fruit.
diseases.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with dark borders; fruit turns brown then shrivels into hard black mummies.
causes: Warm, wet weather.
Mummified fruit and infected wood left in the field.
control: Remove mummies and infected wood; fungicides during susceptible stages per local label.
prevention: Open the canopy by pruning, ensure good drainage, practise sanitation.

diseases.name: Gray leaf spot
diseases.summary: A major leaf disease of maize that reduces grain yield under warm, humid conditions.
diseases.symptoms: Narrow rectangular tan to grey lesions running parallel to the leaf veins.
causes: Warm, humid weather and long leaf wetness.
Maize residue left on the surface, continuous maize.
control: Foliar fungicide at early tassel stage in high-pressure fields, per local label.
prevention: Rotation away from maize, residue tillage, resistant hybrids.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced NPK with adequate potassium; do not leave the crop nitrogen-deficient.

diseases.name: Leaf blight
diseases.agent: Exserohilum turcicum (northern leaf blight of maize) or Pseudocercospora vitis (grape)
diseases.summary: A fungal disease with large leaf lesions that can seriously reduce yield if it appears early.
diseases.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions (maize) or irregular brown spots (grape).
causes: Moderate temperatures with heavy dew or rain.
Infected residue.
control: Foliar fungicide when disease appears early; remove residue.
prevention: Resistant varieties, rotation, residue management.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced NPK; maintain nitrogen and potassium for plant vigour.

diseases.name: Leaf scorch
diseases.summary: A fungal disease of strawberry causing leaf spotting and scorched-looking foliage.
diseases.symptoms: Many small dark purple spots that merge; leaves look scorched.
causes: Wet weather and overhead irrigation.
Infected old leaves.
control: Remove old infected leaves after harvest; fungicides if needed per local label.
prevention: Resistant varieties, drip irrigation, good spacing.

diseases.name: Citrus greening (Huanglongbing)
diseases.agent: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid
diseases.summary: A devastating incurable citrus disease that causes bitter, misshapen fruit and tree decline.
diseases.symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling of leaves, lopsided green fruit, twig dieback.
causes: Feeding by infected psyllids.
Infected budwood or nursery trees.
control: No cure: report to the agricultural authority, remove infected trees, control psyllids.
prevention: Certified disease-free nursery trees, psyllid monitoring and control.
diseases.fertilizer: Balanced nutrition (including micronutrients) may prolong productivity but does not cure the disease.
